text:
Alex: Heads up — seeing p95 spikes on hosted-attn route after the kernel-selector tweak deployed ~10:12 UTC. p95 for seq=1024 workloads jumped from ~210ms -> ~410ms on canary. Canary build: 2026.03.18-xyz
Maria: looking now — is this across all models or just paged/flash combos?
Alex: Mostly models with heavy KV cache hits / long contexts. Quick diff: selector heuristic changed to prefer fused_flash for seq<512, else flash_paged; I'm seeing more flash_paged choices in the 768-1536 range which is where most of the regressions show.
Devon: can we run a perf_bisect between the two commits? i.e., old selector vs new selector. I'll kick one off.
Devon: ```
./infra/tools/perf_bisect --range=commitA..commitB \--bench=attn_latency \--model=redwood-llama-70b \--seqs=256,512,768,1024 \--repeat=10
```
perf-bot: Perf bisect queued: job id 8472. ETA ~18m. Will post results.
Maria: I pulled a GPU profile from the canary run. Attaching a tiny flame snippet — looks like kernel-switch overhead + extra memcpy during KV warmup.
Maria: ```
[flame] time 0.0 | memcpy(32ms) -> flash_paged_kernel(120ms) -> kv_deserialize(40ms)
...
```
Kai: I also noticed batch packing changed after the batching policy tweak: mean batch size shifted from ~6 -> ~9 for multi-turn kv-heavy requests. That increases queueing latency before the kernel runs.
Alex: good call. So could be an interaction: batching heuristics increasing wait + selector choosing a slower path for these batches. Can we isolate by swapping batching vs selector independently?
Devon: I'll run 4 combos on staging: (old_batch,old_selector), (old_batch,new_selector), (new_batch,old_selector), (new_batch,new_selector). Test plan: seq=1024, concurrent=200, client bs sweep 1..16. Will post summary.
perf-bot: job 8472 results:
oldB+oldS p95=210ms
oldB+newS p95=220ms
newB+oldS p95=305ms
newB+newS p95=410ms
(devon-8472-attach)
Maria: that pretty clearly points to batching interacting with selector. new batching increases coalescing -> more flash_paged path invocations -> memcpy + kv warmups add up.
Kai: short-term options: revert batching change, or add a rule to avoid coalescing batches >8 for kv-heavy requests. Also add a small hysteresis to selector so borderline seqs don't flip between kernels quickly.
Alex: ops — what's the impact of rollback? can we flip a flag in canary quickly?
ops: yes we have a feature flag for batching_policy. Can flip in ~2 minutes. Rolling back batching change in canary now.
perf-bot: Feature flag update: batching_policy reverted in canary at 10:40 UTC. Running smoke tests.
Devon: smoke looks good: p95 back to ~215ms. Re-running a full canary ramp for 30m before wider rollback.
Maria: I'll file a bug and add a perf regression eval for seq=1024 kv-heavy that asserts p95<250ms to catch this early. Also adding a kernel-path trace event for selector decisions.
Alex: :thumbsup: good detective work. After canary stabilizes let's land a fix: either tune batching thresholds or add the selector hysteresis plus an integration test.
